observations.seen: Flat-colored box room with line decals; no arcade, no props, no depth.
Every element is a raw primitive (box, cylinder, prism, capsule); no bevels, caps, skirts, rubbers or wireforms.
No textures at all; the playfield has no art, which is the single most important surface in pinball.
Everything is matte single-color plastic; no metal, rubber, glass or lacquer differentiation.
No roughness/metalness variation is readable; flippers and rails show no specular response.
One soft key plus ambient; no GI lights, lamp inserts or neon emission, despite the "neon pinball" pitch.
No cast shadows from posts, bumpers or flippers; objects float.
Uniform ambient fill with no AO in corners, under bumpers or at rail bases.
No environment reflections; a pinball table without a glossy playfield or chrome ball is missing its signature look.
No clipping or crush, but low-contrast and flat, with no HDR highlights to map.
The palette is coherent (slate/cyan/magenta/tan) but desaturated and muddy; the tan/brown elements fight the neon theme.
Edges are reasonably clean at 1080p; the thin rails and line decals show mild stair-stepping.
No bloom, AO, vignette or color grade is evident; the magenta wall gradient is geometry or texture, not post.
The only candidate is a single thin gold ring in one frame.
None visible.
Flipper pose changes are visible; there are no secondary motion cues (bumper pulses, target drops, lamp chases).
The ball is the "hero" and is effectively invisible in every frame.
Shows the whole table legibly but is fully static, too high and too far; the top third is wasted on backdrop.
Symmetric and readable, but the subject is small, the empty grey side decks eat space and the backbox is a dead zone.
No shadows, AO or reflections, so object heights and contacts are hard to read; the table feels like a diorama.
No haze, glow, light shafts or dust; the room has no air.
Layout is readable, but you can't find the ball, and score changes have no in-world feedback.
Clean, consistent dark-card panel; the "0 DOWN 5 TO GO" copy is awkward and the panel is generic web-app UI.
Tidy sans with a warm title accent; generic and with no pinball/DMD flavor.
Three desktop frames are nearly identical despite score changes; zero feedback.
Table is cropped and small, keyboard prompts appear on touch, the button bar overlaps content, and nearly half the screen is stats.
Reads as a programmer-art physics prototype, below the "dated but competent" bar.
